schema_version: case_checklist_v1
case_unit_id: SimpleSmsSend
domain: androidworld
task_id: SimpleSmsSend
native:
  user_goal:
    text: Send an SMS in Simple SMS Messenger to the goal number with the goal message.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/sms.py::SimpleSmsSend
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/task_eval.py::TaskEval.goal
  benchmark_success:
    text: 'Native success requires both: the runner-level completion gate is satisfied (`done=true`), and `SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful` would evaluate to 1.0 from underlying evidence. That evaluator requires a sent-message record for the goal number whose body matches the goal message under the evaluator''s fuzzy string rule and whose `date` is within 5 minutes of the evaluator''s device time, plus Simple SMS Messenger in the foreground at evaluation, with no visible UI element whose text starts with `Sending`.'
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::was_sent
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::_check_if_stuck_at_sending
  checked_by:
    text: AndroidWorld runner completion gating in `suite_utils._run_task` together with `android_world.task_evals.common_validators.sms_validators.SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful`.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful
  decisive_artifacts:
  - artifact: Retained dispatched goal or task params
    question: What exact recipient number and message body did this run require?
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/sms.py::SimpleSmsSend
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/task_eval.py::TaskEval.goal
  - artifact: Retained end-of-run sent-SMS evidence plus retained device-time evidence
    question: At evaluation time, is there a sent-SMS row (or equivalent telephony DB/query snapshot) whose address equals the goal number after removing spaces/dashes, whose body matches the goal message under the evaluator's fuzzy rule, and whose `date` is within 5 minutes of the retained device time?
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.get_sent_messages
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.get_android_time
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::was_sent
  - artifact: Retained end-of-run foreground-activity and UI-state evidence
    question: At evaluation time, was the foreground package `com.simplemobiletools.smsmessenger`, and did the visible UI lack any element whose text starts with `Sending`?
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::_check_if_stuck_at_sending
  - artifact: Retained completion evidence from the episode trace
    question: Did the episode finish with `done=true` rather than ending unfinished?
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
  success_if:
  - text: Success if the retained goal/params identify the expected number and message, retained completion evidence shows `done=true`, retained sent-SMS plus device-time evidence satisfies `was_sent` for that number/message, and retained end-of-run activity/UI evidence shows `com.simplemobiletools.smsmessenger` in the foreground with no visible `Sending` element.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::was_sent
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::_check_if_stuck_at_sending
  fail_if:
  - text: Fail if retained completion evidence shows `done=false`.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
  - text: Fail if retained goal/params and retained sent-SMS plus device-time evidence show there is no qualifying recent sent row for the goal number/message under `was_sent`, including when the only matching row is older than the evaluator's 5-minute window.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::was_sent
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful
  - text: Fail if retained end-of-run foreground-activity evidence shows a package other than `com.simplemobiletools.smsmessenger`.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful
  - text: Fail if retained end-of-run UI evidence shows any visible element whose text starts with `Sending`.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::_check_if_stuck_at_sending
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful
  undecided_if:
  - text: Undecided if the retained evidence does not preserve the dispatched number/message, or lacks a usable end-of-run sent-SMS snapshot/query with message date and retained device time, or lacks usable end-of-run foreground/UI evidence, and the remaining retained evidence does not already establish one of the listed fail conditions.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.get_sent_messages
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.get_android_time
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
stronger:
  additional_conditions:
  - id: exact_message_body_match
    text: Because the official task asks for the specified message, require the sent SMS body to equal the goal message exactly, not merely match under the native evaluator's fuzzy string rule.
    rationale: 'This is a concrete evaluator gap: the task template specifies the message itself, while native scoring accepts approximate body matches through `fuzzy_match` in `was_sent`.'
    decisive_artifacts:
    - artifact: Retained dispatched goal or task params
      question: What exact message body did the run require?
      support:
      - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/sms.py::SimpleSmsSend
      - official/install/android_world/task_evals/task_eval.py::TaskEval.goal
    - artifact: Retained sent-SMS row or equivalent telephony snapshot
      question: Does the sent SMS body equal the goal message exactly for the qualifying message to the goal number?
      support:
      - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::was_sent
      - official/install/android_world/utils/fuzzy_match_lib.py::fuzzy_match
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/sms.py::SimpleSmsSend
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::was_sent
    - official/install/android_world/utils/fuzzy_match_lib.py::fuzzy_match

General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.

- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.

Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.

General

Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.

Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.
- For `click`, `long_press` and `input_text`, the index parameter you pick must be VISIBLE in the screenshot and also in the UI element list given to you (some elements in the list may NOT be visible on the screen so you can not interact with them).
- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.
- The direction parameter for the `scroll` action can be confusing sometimes as it's opposite to swipe, for example, to view content at the bottom, the `scroll` direction should be set to "down". It has been observed that you have difficulties in choosing the correct direction, so if one does not work, try the opposite as well.
Text Related Operations

Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.
- For `click`, `long_press` and `input_text`, the index parameter you pick must be VISIBLE in the screenshot and also in the UI element list given to you (some elements in the list may NOT be visible on the screen so you can not interact with them).
- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.
- The direction parameter for the `scroll` action can be confusing sometimes as it's opposite to swipe, for example, to view content at the bottom, the `scroll` direction should be set to "down". It has been observed that you have difficulties in choosing the correct direction, so if one does not work, try the opposite as well.
Text Related Operations
- Normally to select some text on the screen: <i> Enter text selection mode by long pressing the area where the text is, then some of the words near the long press point will be selected (highlighted with two pointers indicating the range) and usually a text selection bar will also appear with options like `copy`, `paste`, `select all`, etc. <ii> Select the exact text you need. Usually the text selected from the previous step is NOT the one you want, you need to adjust the range by dragging the two pointers. If you want to select all text in the text field, simply click the `select all` button in the bar.
- At this point, you don't have the ability to drag something around the screen, so in general you can not select arbitrary text.
- To delete some text: the most traditional way is to place the cursor at the right place and use the backspace button in the keyboard to delete the characters one by one (can long press the backspace to accelerate if there are many to delete). Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.
